metadata.note: The Kentucky Central system: the Covington and Lexington Railroad (Covington - Paris - Lexington, opened 1853-56), its successor the Kentucky Central (1859/61-1891; Railroad to 1887, Railway after) with the Maysville branch and the 1883-85 Paris - Winchester - Richmond - Livingston extension and its lease of the L&N Richmond (Rowland) Branch, and the same lines under the Louisville and Nashville from 1891 to the end of the last Cincinnati - Atlanta train on 7 Mar 1968. Research report: research/branches/kentucky_central_railway.txt.
sources: https://archive.org/details/the-official-guide-of-the-railways-images (Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952; full text in research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)

metadata.operator_split: Covington - Paris: C&L 1856-1859 | Kentucky Central 1859-1891 | L&N 1891-1968 (L&N part of ln-cincinnati-knoxville-via-paris). Paris - Lexington: C&L 1854-1859 | KC 1859-1891 | L&N 1891-1917 [OPEN]. Paris - Maysville: (1873-1875 undrawn, operator unsettled) | KC 1876-1891 | L&N 1891-1936. Paris - Richmond: KC 1883-1891 | L&N 1891-1968. Richmond - Livingston: KC 1885-1891 | L&N 1891-1968. Richmond - Rowland: L&N 1868-1882 | (1882-1883 undrawn, lease-date conflict) | KC lessee 1884-1890 | nothing after 1891. The L&N main-line feature is the three KC main-line geometries joined end to end. New colours: Covington and Lexington #D9822B, Kentucky Central #1E8C7E (no company in data/ used either); L&N #7A4419 pulled from the existing L&N features.
omitted: Report block [9], Kentucky Central operation of Lexington - Nicholasville for the City of Cincinnati 1873-1877: deferred to research/branches/cincinnati_southern_railway.txt, which holds it pending a dated listing.
Paris - Maysville 1873-1875: trains ran but the operator (Maysville and Lexington Northern Division vs the C&L as lessee) is unsettled; see kc-paris-maysville.
Richmond - Rowland 1882-1883 (lease-date conflict) and the whole branch after 1891 (no dated passenger listing; freight-only by 1951).
Covington - Paris 1854-1855 and Covington - Falmouth 1853/54-1855 (opening-date conflict; latest date taken).
All freight-only years: Paris - Maysville after 1936, Lancaster - Rowland to 1979, the main line after 7 Mar 1968 (CSX).
The Cincinnati approach over the C&O Ohio River bridge (1888 on) - track drawn by other layers.
not_yet_sourced: ln-paris-lexington end [OPEN]: passenger service confirmed only to 1917 (WWI, NRHP Carlisle nomination); no source dates the actual end. Could be 1936 with the Maysville trains or later.

Paris - Maysville operator 1873-c.1876 (M&L Northern Division vs C&L lessee) and the date the Kentucky Central took over working it - ICC Valuation (L&N; Maysville & Lexington RR North Division) or Herr pp.114-120.
Maysville branch passenger end: 1936 (NRHP) vs Fowler "1939t" listings; a Maysville/Carlisle newspaper "last train" story would settle it.
Covington - Paris opening: 1854 (Lexhistory, 1876 Paris history) vs 1856 (Wikipedia CC Subdivision).

Paris - Livingston extension: completed 1883 (Wikipedia) vs 1885 (Lexhistory); Paris - Richmond drawn from 1883, Richmond - Livingston from 1885. kc-paris-richmond from 1883 predates the drawn 1884 start of the Rowland-branch lease the KC used for Richmond - Fort Estill.
Rowland Branch lease start: 1 Jun 1882 (Abandoned Online) vs 1884 (Lexhistory); post-1891 passenger end unknown.
L&N operating hand-over: control 1890, "took over" Dec 1890, sale 22 Sep 1891 - drawn as 1891.
All headways and speeds are estimates.

segments.note: Covington and Lexington main line, Covington - Falmouth - Cynthiana - Paris. Opening year conflicts: Lexhistory (S3) has Covington - Falmouth Oct 1853 and Covington - Paris complete with regular trains May 1854, and an 1876 Paris history (S8) has the first train into Paris in "the Fall of 1854"; the CC Subdivision article (S4) has only 20 mi built by 1853 and Paris reached in 1856. Drawn from 1856, the latest of the conflicting dates (report block [1]; years 1854-1855 withheld, not denied). Fowler's 1858 Dinsmore letters (S2) at Grant's Bend, Kiser's, Boyd's, Berry's, Robertson's and Garnett's confirm trains by 1858. Ends 1859, when the company was sold at auction (Oct 1859, S3); continues as kc-covington-paris. Headway is an estimate (about one train each way a day); no C&L timetable was read.

segments.note: Kentucky Central main line. The C&L was auctioned in Oct 1859 and its assets taken by the Kentucky Central Railroad Association, formally constituted 1 Jan 1861 (S3; S4 gives 1859). Same operator throughout, through the 1874-75 receivership, the Jan 1886 bankruptcy and the 7 Jun 1887 reorganisation as the Kentucky Central Railway (S3); Huntington control c.1881-1890 was stock control, not a change of operator. Confederate raiders burned the Cynthiana depot and bridges in 1862 (S3) - an interruption of unknown length, not trimmed. Standard gauge from 10 Jul 1881 (S3). Fowler's 1875 Official Guide letter (S2) at Covington, South Covington, Falmouth, Cynthiana, Paris and 18 other stations confirms 1875. Ends 1891 with the sale to the L&N (L&N held two-thirds of the stock from 1890; remaining shares 22 Sep 1891, S3/S4); the operating hand-over may have been Dec 1890. Continues as ln-cincinnati-knoxville-via-paris. Headway is an estimate (about three trains each way a day); no KC timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: research report research/branches/kentucky_central_railway.txt block [3] - S3 (1859 auction, 1861 Association, 1891 sale), S4 (1859, 1890 control, 22 Sep 1891), S2 (1875G station letters), S5. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Maysville branch. Built by the Maysville and Lexington Railroad, Northern Division: to Carlisle by 1871 and Maysville two years later (S5); first Maysville - Lexington train March 1872, completed 1873 (S3). The NRHP Carlisle depot nomination (S5, citing Herr pp.114-120) says that "in 1876 the Lexington and Maysville Railroad was purchased by the Kentucky Central Railroad", and this feature is drawn from that year. 1873-1875 ARE DELIBERATELY UNDRAWN: trains certainly ran (Fowler's 1875 Official Guide letters at Millersburg, Carlisle, Ewing, Maysville and five other stations, S2), but who ran them is unsettled - S5 has the Northern Division leased to the Covington and Lexington, while the 1876 Paris history (S8) lists "the Maysville and Lexington, running from Maysville to this city" as a separate railroad with its own agent, and the North Division company existed 1876-1921. Even after 1876 the KC's operation is inferred from S5 rather than a dated timetable. Ends 1891 with the L&N purchase; continues as ln-maysville-branch. Headway is an estimate; no timetable was read.

Richmond - Fort Estill on L&N-tagged track (CC Subdivision / abandoned L&N branch ways), Fort Estill - Duncannon on abandoned L&N ways, then Silver Creek - Paint Lick - Lancaster - Rowland on abandoned L&N-tagged ways ("L&N Rowland Branch", "Old Railroad Grade Road" and unnamed railway=abandoned), ending at the Lebanon Branch junction east of Stanford (37.532N 84.638W). Total 1.1 mi (3%) over the documented figure, mostly the Richmond end, which starts at the common Richmond point rather than at the branch's own 1868 Richmond terminal (not located).

segments.note: The L&N Richmond (Rowland) Branch, Richmond - Fort Estill - Paint Lick - Lancaster - Rowland, worked by the Kentucky Central under lease from the L&N, which the KC used for Fort Estill - Richmond as part of its main line. Lease start conflicts: 1 Jun 1882 (Abandoned Online, S6, citing Herr and Sulzer) vs 1884 for a 34-mile Richmond - Stanford lease (Lexhistory, S3). Drawn from 1884, the later date (report block [8]); 1882-1883 withheld, not denied - Fowler's "Stanford Junction + 1883G", a name used on the KC only (S2), suggests 1882/83 is right. S6: "daily round-trip passenger train services between Louisville and Cincinnati" over the branch for several years, plus a Richmond - Stanford local. Ends 1890: the lease ended in Dec 1890 when the L&N took over the KC (S6). Nothing is drawn after that - no post-1891 passenger year has been found for the branch (Lancaster - Fort Estill traffic ceased 1932, abandoned 1934; Lancaster - Rowland freight-only in the Feb 1952 Official Guide, last train 1979). Headway is an estimate; no timetable was read.

segments.note: The former Kentucky Central main line under the L&N, Covington - Paris - Winchester - Richmond - Livingston, the northern part of the L&N's Cincinnati - Knoxville - Atlanta route. L&N from the 1891 purchase (control 1890; remaining shares 22 Sep 1891, S3/S4). Trains included the Flamingo (Cincinnati - Jacksonville via Atlanta from 27 Sep 1925, stops Covington, Latonia, Falmouth, Cynthiana, Paris, Winchester, Richmond, Berea; cut back to Atlanta 1962, unnamed from 1965) and the Southland. The July 1951 Official Guide (S1, L&N Table 12) shows three southbound departures from Cincinnati and a northbound Winchester 6:04 - Paris 6:27 - Cincinnati 9:25. Ends with the discontinuance of the last Cincinnati - Atlanta train on 7 Mar 1968 (S7; corroborated by chicagorailfan.com and Wikipedia "Paris Depot"). Freight continues as the CSX CC Subdivision - not drawn. Headway is an estimate (about four trains each way a day in the 1940s-50s, fewer at the end).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 18.3 mi against 19.2 mi documented (Fowler (S2) L&N line 2: Paris - Lexington 19.2). Paris - Lexington on L&N-tagged OSM ways (14.6 mi, incl. the abandoned grade and the surviving R.J. Corman/L&N track at the Lexington end) plus OpenHistoricalMap ways where OSM has nothing (3.6 mi untagged OHM rail of 1853, Paris - Hutchison side), and the last 0.4 mi into Lexington along OHM "Maysville & Lexington R.R." ways (-201076791, -201076047/8, -201076044, -201070688/9/90) to the old terminal at 38.0528N 84.5067W. No straight-line legs; a 0.3 mi link at Paris joins the common Paris point on the CC Subdivision. OHM "Maysville & Lexington R.R." ways: median 2 m from the drawn line. LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTE: the Lexington end is drawn to OHM's terminal of the 1853 line; the 1882 Water St station and, for 1907-on, Lexington Union Station (Main St) were not separately located, so the last few hundred metres may not match the station of every era.

segments.note: Paris - Lexington under the L&N from 1891 (S3). Passenger service confirmed to 1917 by the NRHP Carlisle depot nomination (S5): during the First World War there were "eight daily passenger trains operating between Lexington, Paris and Maysville". [OPEN] THIS IS THE LAST CONFIRMED YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END - no source dates when passenger trains between Paris and Lexington actually stopped. They may have ended with the Maysville trains in 1936, or continued later with Cincinnati - Lexington locals; Wikipedia's Lexington Union Station article (S9) does not list them, and Lexhistory's c.1951 abandonment of the Paris line (S3) is an abandonment date, not a passenger end. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate (from the WWI eight-a-day figure, which covers Lexington - Paris - Maysville together).

segments.note: Paris - Millersburg - Carlisle - Ewing - Maysville under the L&N from 1891 (the line stayed a Maysville and Lexington RR North Division company until the L&N bought it in 1921 - a corporate, not an operating, change). WWI: "eight daily passenger trains operating between Lexington, Paris and Maysville" (S5). Ends 1936: "Passenger service continued until 1936 when the L and N discontinued it" (NRHP Carlisle depot nomination, S5, citing Herr). Conflicts recorded: Fowler lists "Tarr 1939t" and "Miller 1939t" on this line (S2); an Aug 1951 Flemingsburg & Northern table prints a Maysville/Paris/Lexington connection (S1) - but the L&N's own Feb 1952 Guide lists "PARIS AND MAYSVILLE" (Table 55) under "STATIONS SERVED WITH FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY" (S1). Drawn to 1936, the earliest end; freight continued (today the Transkentucky Transportation Railroad) and is not drawn. Headway is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 34.6 mi against 33.5 mi documented (Fowler (S2) L&N line 10, Rowland Branch: Rowland 33.5; S6 "33-mile"). Richmond - Fort Estill on L&N-tagged track (CC Subdivision / abandoned L&N branch ways), Fort Estill - Duncannon on abandoned L&N ways, then Silver Creek - Paint Lick - Lancaster - Rowland on abandoned L&N-tagged ways ("L&N Rowland Branch", "Old Railroad Grade Road" and unnamed railway=abandoned), ending at the Lebanon Branch junction east of Stanford (37.532N 84.638W). STRAIGHT-LINE LEG: one, 2.5 mi, west of Fort Estill between the end of the mapped abandoned grade at 37.6819N 84.2761W and its resumption at 37.6703N 84.3215W - no OSM railway, trail or OHM way survives there. Total 1.1 mi (3%) over the documented figure, mostly the Richmond end, which starts at the common Richmond point rather than at the branch's own 1868 Richmond terminal (not located).

segments.note: The L&N Richmond Branch (later the Rowland Branch, "Old Henry" after its mixed train), Rowland - Lancaster - Paint Lick - Fort Estill - Richmond, completed 8 Nov 1868 with an excursion train to Richmond the same day (Abandoned Online, S6, citing Herr and Sulzer). Fowler's Official Guide letters (S2): "Hayden's 1868G", "Gilbert's 1870G", "Moran's Summit 1874G", and 1875G at Duncannon, Silver Creek, Paint Lick, Lancaster, Richmond Junction and others. Ends 1882: leased to the Kentucky Central from 1 Jun 1882 (S6) - see kc-richmond-rowland, which is drawn only from 1884 because the lease date conflicts. NOT DRAWN AFTER 1891: no dated post-1891 passenger listing has been found for the branch (report block [14]). Mixed trains count as passenger service. Headway is an estimate; no timetable was read.
